holidays.name: National Pretzel Day
holidays.description: A salty, twisty celebration of one of the world's favorite snacks. Pretzels get their due, whether they're soft and buttery, hard and crunchy, or dunked in mustard or cheese.
holidays.origin: Pretzels are traditionally linked to European monasteries, where bakers are said to have shaped dough to look like arms crossed in prayer. The day itself is an unofficial observance, and it is listed on April 26.
holidays.funFact: The pretzel's knot shape is often said to resemble folded arms in prayer, and the word 'pretzel' may come from the Latin 'bracchiola', meaning 'little arms'.

holidays.name: Alien Day
holidays.description: A fan holiday for the Alien movie franchise. Sci-fi fans celebrate the xenomorph, the Nostromo crew, and the chest-bursting scares with movie marathons, screenings, and themed parties.
holidays.origin: The date comes from LV-426, the fictional moon where the crew first encounters the xenomorph in the Alien films. Read as a date, 4/26 matches the name. Fans began marking it in 2015, and the studio embraced it afterward.
holidays.funFact: The moon is named LV-426, and 4/26 is the date that matches it. The fans who spotted the connection turned a bit of fictional planetary bookkeeping into a yearly holiday.

holidays.name: Hug an Australian Day
holidays.description: A friendly day for sharing a hug with an Aussie in your life, or for tracking one down. Mates, neighbors, and visiting travelers all count.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin that is listed on April 26.
holidays.funFact: Australia is home to more than 250 million kangaroos by some estimates, so the country has plenty of other huggable residents too, though they may not want a hug.
